title: Restore drills: how often, and measuring how long it actually took

videos.script: Every restore in this course so far was a demonstration. One person, a quiet machine, and the answer known in advance. {{demo}} A restore drill is the same act, made into a routine. The newest backup, restored somewhere harmless, proved, timed and thrown away. {{routine}} First you write a report that finds the tables by itself, so next month's new table is in next month's drill. {{report}} Then a script that does the whole drill, unattended, and writes one line of history. {{script}} You run it while something writes, and it fails, with a perfect backup. {{fail}} A drill that fails for its own reasons teaches people to ignore it. So you fix how it reads the two sides. {{moment}} Last, the arithmetic. How often to drill, and why the answer depends on how long your backups are kept. {{often}}
